item.title: Comment on Make Sunsets: Geoengineering by Heydocbrowm
item.description:
I know the geoengineering community very well. Make Sunsets is considered dumb cowboys. The challenge with sulfur engineering is not getting it into the atmosphere, it’s understanding its effects because they’re highly regional. If you do it at scale in you’ll overcool that region which will disrupt global weather.

I would suggest looking instead at the Israeli startup Stardust, which has created a molecule that cools but doesn’t cause acid rain and is working diligently at atmospheric modeling.

Silver Linings is a non-profit that funds and advocates for the capacity to do geoengineering effectively.

Alex, I’m happy to make intros for you to these and others, if you’d like to dive deeper into this field.

item.title: Comment on Congestion pricing update by Jonathan
item.description:
Wow did Tyler even read the article, or just pull out the one negative quote? The rest of it talks about how buses are packed as people shift to public transit, bus commutes are much faster, and bus companies are adding buses to increase supply. This is a clear victory for efficiency. Maybe he’s just being “Straussian” in his dogged opposition to this improvement.
